resale_co.name: Certificate of Inspection for Resale (resale certificate of occupancy)
resale_co.issued_by: Borough of Woodlynne Construction Official (form); the Borough code also calls for a zoning certificate of occupancy from the Zoning Officer on a change of occupants by sale
requirements: Inspection for resale, marked pass or fail by the Construction Official
Any building, plumbing, electrical or fire permits the Construction Official requires must be completed before the final Certificate of Occupancy
Under the Borough code, the new owner must get a certificate of occupancy from the Zoning Officer showing the intended use meets Borough zoning

fees.label: Application for Certificate of Inspection for Resale

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Certificate of Inspection for Resale (building address, owner, agent or contractor, email) and return it to the Borough of Woodlynne, 200 Cooper Ave., Woodlynne, NJ 08107, or fax it to 856-962-8763. Contact Bill Lunemann at 856-962-8300 ext. 219.
resale_co.contact_title: Contact named on the resale application (no title shown)

evidence.quote: Application for Certificate of Inspection for Resale
PERMIT(S) REQUIRED FOR FINAL CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY

Whenever any premises will suffer a change of occupants, by reason of sale or lease of same, the new owner or lessor thereof must apply for and obtain a certificate of occupancy from the Zoning Officer certifying that the intended use of the premises conforms to the zoning regulations of the Borough of Woodlynne.

resale_co.notes: The Borough posted a new resale application on its Code Enforcement and Fire Department pages (PDF created September 30, 2026). The fee is still $96.00, but the contact changed from David Munoz (woodlynnedavid@comcast.net) to Bill Lunemann, William.lunemann@woodlynne.org, ext. 219; the email uses woodlynne.org, not the woodlynnenj.org website domain, so confirm it. The form is a scanned image, so quotes were read from the page image and may not be machine-checkable. It lists no inspection checklist, validity period, lead time or re-inspection fee. Borough code section 480-2A(1) (read on ecode360) requires the new owner to get a zoning certificate of occupancy on a change of occupants by sale; for 4 or more units a separate property maintenance CO is also needed. Code chapter 526 still sets a $25 Borough smoke detector inspection fee before sale (Ord. 1989-1), but smoke certificates are now handled by NJ DCA, so that fee is not listed. Woodlynne also runs a rental program (Chapter 494 and a rental application on the same page); that is not a resale requirement.

requirements: Smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms as required by N.J.A.C. 5:70-4.19 for 1 and 2 family homes (the Borough and DCA pages found do not list the details)

authorities.name: NJ Department of Community Affairs, Division of Fire Safety, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement
authorities.lead_time: Fee depends on how many business days before the change of occupant the request is received: more than 10 business days for the lowest fee.

fees.label: Request received 4 to 10 business days before the change of occupant

authorities.how_to_apply: Apply, schedule and pay online through the NJ DCA fire service portal (firesolutions.dca.nj.gov), using 'Apply for Smoke Certification'.
authorities.contact_title: Bureau Chief, Bureau of Fire Code Enforcement (listed as the state fire official for this town in the DCA fire directory)

fire_cert.notes: The DCA state-towns list (revised 7/17/2026), the July 2026 LEA registry (code S) and the DCA fire directory (LEAID 0437-999, State) all show NJ DCA issues smoke/CO certificates in Woodlynne. The Borough website has no smoke certificate page. Fees are the state fees in N.J.A.C. 5:70-2.9(d) as published in the NJ Register (50 N.J.R. 729(a)). Borough code chapter 526 still describes a $25 local smoke detector inspection before sale; it appears superseded by state enforcement. The 2025 state law (P.L.2025, c.19) dropped the portable fire extinguisher from the sale certificate.

other_items.label: Zoning certificate of occupancy
other_items.detail: On a change of occupants by sale, the new owner must get a certificate of occupancy from the Zoning Officer confirming the use meets Borough zoning (Code section 480-2A(1)). It may be the same document as the resale certificate; confirm with the Borough.

other_items.label: Open permits
other_items.detail: Any building, plumbing, electrical or fire permits the Construction Official requires must be completed before the final Certificate of Occupancy.
